newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal welcomes Nobel award to Timor activists.
newsitem.headline: Portugal welcomes Nobel award to Timor activists.

text.p: Portuguese President Jorge Sampaio welcomed on Friday the award of the 1996 Nobel peace prize to Bishop Carlos Belo and Jose Ramos-Horta for their work towards a peaceful solution in the former Portuguese territory East Timor.
"The award reflects their indefatigable work in the service of human rights and peace in the territory," Sampaio told reporters. "I am very pleased by the news. It is a wonderful surprise."
Portugal and Indonesia have been at loggerheads over East Timor since Indonesia invaded the former Portuguese colony in 1975 and subsequently annexed it in defiance of the United Nations.
The U.N. still recognises Lisbon as the administering power.
Ramos-Horta is spokesman for East Timorese resistance leader Xanana Gusmao, who is serving a 20-year jail sentence in Indonesia.
Belo, East Timor's outspoken and often fiery Roman Catholic bishop, is long used to walking a tightrope between his flock and the Indonesian government.
